context.analysis:
## Overview
[Library Management System] is a solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals, adhering strictly to EU-only data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
* Patrons (Self-service portal users)
* Staff and Librarians
* System Administrator / Operations
* Library Management System (Core Software System)
* Legacy ILS / Campus ERP Systems
* Identity Providers and Payment Gateways
* Edge / WAF (Web Application Firewall)
* Enterprise Logging and Monitoring Service
* EU-Hosted Backup and Archival Storage
* Network Time Protocol (NTP) service

## Relationships
* Patrons interact with Library Management System via HTTPS through Edge/WAF
* Staff and Librarians access core domain services via HTTPS
* Library Management System syncs with Legacy ILS / ERP via REST/SOAP APIs
* Library Management System integrates with Identity Providers via OAuth2/OIDC
* System communicates with EU-hosted Backup Storage via encrypted transport protocols

## Technology Stack
* Edge / WAF for DDoS protection and latency optimization
* OAuth2/OIDC for identity federation
* REST/SOAP APIs for enterprise system integration
* EU-hosted infrastructure for backup and archival storage

## Rationale
The architecture strictly enforces EU data residency by bounding all third-party integrations, backups, and audit trails to EU infrastructure. It guarantees sub-800ms search performance through Edge/WAF protection, decoupled high-throughput user interactions, and clear actor boundary separation.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for academic and public libraries. It ensures EU-only data residency and sub-800ms search responses.

## Key Elements
* Patrons, Staff, Librarians, and System Administrators
* API Gateway / BFF Container
* Web App & Core Transactional Service Containers
* Search Service Container (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch)
* Message Broker Container (RabbitMQ/Kafka)
* Distributed Cache Container (Redis)
* Worker / Background Task Container
* Observability Sidecars
* External Legacy ILS, Identity Providers, Payment Gateways, and WAF

## Relationships
* Patrons and Staff communicate via HTTPS to the API Gateway Container.
* API Gateway routes requests to Web App and Core Transactional Service via internal REST/gRPC.
* Core Transactional Service publishes events to Message Broker via AMQP/Kafka protocol.
* Search Service consumes events and indexes catalog data, serving queries via HTTP.
* Workers sync with Legacy ILS and ERP systems using scheduled batch protocols.

## Technology Stack
* Elasticsearch / OpenSearch: Chosen for the Search Service to meet the < 800 ms p99 latency requirement (R-05).
* Redis: Used as a distributed cache to maintain stateless application tiers and ensure fast data access.
* RabbitMQ or Kafka: Implemented as an Asynchronous Event Bus to decouple writes and maintain indexing consistency.
* Kubernetes: Orchestrator enforcing resource quotas, health checks, and strict EU-region deployments.

## Rationale
Decoupling search and background processing from core transactions protects system performance under load. Strict EU region hosting and stateless container designs ensure data residency compliance and scalability.

API Gateway / BFF Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. The architecture utilizes an API Gateway/BFF pattern to handle client requests, secure traffic, and meet strict EU data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
- Users: Patrons, Staff, Librarians, and System Administrators
- Edge Security: Edge / WAF
- Gateway: API Gateway / BFF Container
- Core Services: Web App Container, Core Transactional Service Container, Search Service Container
- Infrastructure: Distributed Cache Container (Redis), Message Broker Container (Kafka/RabbitMQ)

## Relationships
- Patrons/Staff/Librarians/Administrators -> API Gateway / BFF Container: HTTPS [HTTPS]
- Edge / WAF -> API Gateway / BFF Container: Inspects and filters traffic [HTTPS]
- API Gateway / BFF Container -> Core Transactional Service Container: Routes requests [Internal REST/gRPC]
- API Gateway / BFF Container -> Search Service Container: Routes search queries [Internal REST/gRPC]
- API Gateway / BFF Container -> Distributed Cache Container (Redis): Offloads session state and caching [TCP]

## Technology Stack
- API Gateway / BFF: Custom routing engine with declarative configuration for maintainability
- Authentication: OAuth2/OIDC integrated via gateway
- Caching/Session State: Redis for horizontal scalability and session offloading
- Search: Elasticsearch / OpenSearch for sub-800ms catalogue retrieval
- Contracts: OpenAPI/Swagger for API schema definition and automated testing

## Rationale
This architecture ensures horizontal scalability and sub-800ms search performance through distributed caching and request optimization at the gateway. Strict data residency and security constraints are met via edge filtering, PII log sanitization, and OAuth2 validation.

Web App Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries within an EU-only data residency constraint. It utilizes a containerized microservices architecture to ensure high performance, meeting 99th-percentile search response times under 800 ms.

## Key Elements
- Web App Container (Web Application Framework)
- API Gateway / BFF Container (API Gateway / BFF)
- Search Service Container (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch)
- Distributed Cache Container (Redis)
- Enterprise Logging and Monitoring Service

## Relationships
- API Gateway / BFF Container -> Web App Container: Routes requests [Internal REST/gRPC]
- Web App Container -> Search Service Container: Serves search queries [HTTP]
- Web App Container -> Distributed Cache Container: Manages sessions and caches catalogue queries [Redis Protocol]
- Web App Container -> Enterprise Logging and Monitoring Service: Sends structured JSON logs and metrics [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Server-Side Rendering (SSR) with Hydration: Balances SEO for catalogues with UI interactivity
- Redis: Externalizes session state for stateless container scalability
- Structured JSON Logging: Streamlines ingestion into enterprise monitoring

## Rationale
The architecture ensures strict EU data compliance while maintaining horizontal scalability and low latency. Stateless containers combined with distributed caching and optimized rendering directly support the required high-performance search targets.

Core Transactional Service Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items and manage circulation. The architecture utilizes a containerized microservices approach centered around a Core Transactional Service Container to handle business logic.

## Key Elements
- API Gateway / BFF Container
- Core Transactional Service Container (Microservice / REST / gRPC)
- Search Service Container (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch)
- Message Broker Container (RabbitMQ / Kafka)
- Distributed Cache Container (Redis)
- Worker / Background Task Container
- EU-Hosted Relational Database

## Relationships
- API Gateway / BFF Container -> Core Transactional Service Container: Routes requests [Internal gRPC/REST]
- Core Transactional Service Container -> Message Broker Container: Publishes events [AMQP/Kafka]
- Core Transactional Service Container -> Distributed Cache Container: Caches and retrieves fast data [Redis Protocol]
- Core Transactional Service Container -> EU-Hosted Relational Database: Persists core transactions [SQL/ORM]

## Technology Stack
- gRPC / Protobuf: Internal service-to-service communication for strong typing and performance
- Transactional Outbox Pattern: Ensures reliable event publishing without dual-write inconsistencies
- Domain-Driven Design (DDD): Modular monolith boundaries within the service for circulation and cataloguing
- Optimistic Concurrency Control: Handles high-contention item checkouts via version columns
- W3C Trace Context: Distributed tracing standards for latency and bottleneck analysis

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict EU-only data residency while maintaining high availability and low latency. Resiliency patterns and modular boundaries protect core circulation workflows from cascading failures.

Search Service Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides a solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and offer self-service portals with strict EU-only data residency. The Search Service Container delivers fast, scalable search functionality ensuring 99th-percentile search responses under 800ms.

## Key Elements
* Search Service Container (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch)
* Message Broker Container (RabbitMQ / Kafka)
* Web App Container (Web Application Framework)
* Distributed Cache Container (Redis)
* Enterprise Logging and Monitoring Service
* EU-Hosted Backup and Archival Storage

## Relationships
* Message Broker Container -> Search Service Container: Consumes events for indexing [Asynchronous Message Stream]
* Web App Container -> Search Service Container: Serves search queries [HTTP]
* Search Service Container -> Distributed Cache Container: Caches frequent catalogue lookups [TCP]
* Search Service Container -> EU-Hosted Backup and Archival Storage: Stores automated index snapshots [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* Elasticsearch / OpenSearch: Chosen for fast, scalable search capabilities ensuring sub-800ms 99th-percentile response times.
* RabbitMQ / Kafka: Used for decoupled asynchronous event-driven ingestion to prevent database write bottlenecks.
* Redis: Implements result caching to offload the search cluster and protect latency SLAs.
* JSON Schema / Protocol Buffers: Enforces strict schema validation at the ingestion boundary to prevent payload corruption.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples heavy write ingestion from user-facing queries using asynchronous messaging and read/write segregation, ensuring high availability and performance. Strict EU data residency constraints and disaster recovery procedures are enforced through isolated backups and automated compliance tooling.

Rel(Search_Engine_Core, Backup_Service, "Triggers automated index snapshots", "HTTPS")
@enduml

Message Broker Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items and manage circulation. It uses an asynchronous message broker architecture to decouple writes and maintain indexing consistency.

## Key Elements
- Message Broker Container (RabbitMQ / Kafka)
- Core Transactional Service Container
- Search Service Container (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch)
- Schema Registry
- Observability Sidecar
- EU-Hosted Object Storage

## Relationships
- Core Transactional Service Container -> Message Broker Container: Publishes events [AMQP/Kafka protocol]
- Message Broker Container -> Search Service Container: Consumes events for indexing [Asynchronous Message Stream]

## Technology Stack
- RabbitMQ / Kafka: Decouples write operations and ensures search indexing performance under 800 ms
- Avro or JSON Schema: Enforces strict payload contracts via a schema registry
- EU-Hosted Object Storage: Stores large digital item payloads via reference pointers to prevent broker memory bloat

## Rationale
This architecture ensures high performance and strict EU-only data residency compliance. Asynchronous messaging protects search response times while robust broker governance guarantees system reliability.
Message Broker Container.yaml_definition:
level: component
scope: "Component diagram for the Message Broker Container container"
parentContainer:
  name: "Message Broker Container"
elements:
  - type: "component"
    name: "Event Publisher Receiver"
    technology: "RabbitMQ / Kafka"
    description: "Receives and decouples write operations from the Core Transactional Service."
  - type: "component"
    name: "Event Stream Dispatcher"
    technology: "Asynchronous Message Stream"
    description: "Consumes and streams events to the Search Service Container for indexing."
relationships:
  - source: "Event Publisher Receiver"
    destination: "Event Stream Dispatcher"
    description: "Routes and dispatches events for search indexing"

Distributed Cache Container.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a Library Management System providing cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals with strict EU data residency. The architecture utilizes a Distributed Cache Container to maintain stateless application tiers and meet sub-800ms search performance.

## Key Elements
- Distributed Cache Container: Redis
- Core Transactional Service Container
- Enterprise Logging and Monitoring Service
- Kubernetes Orchestrator

## Relationships
- Core Transactional Service Container -> Distributed Cache Container: Caches and retrieves fast data [Redis Protocol with TLS]
- Distributed Cache Container -> Enterprise Logging and Monitoring Service: Exports telemetry and metrics

## Technology Stack
- Redis: Chosen for high-throughput, low-latency caching to satisfy the <800ms performance requirement.
- AOF/RDB Persistence: Configured on EU-hosted storage volumes for data residency compliance.
- Resilience4j / Polly: Implemented for connection pooling and circuit breaking.
- Protocol Buffers / Compressed JSON: Used for efficient payload serialization.
- Testcontainers: Used for automated integration testing of caching logic.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict EU data residency while providing robust, high-performance caching mechanisms. Circuit breakers, cache stampede prevention, and failover strategies protect the system under high loads to maintain the 99th-percentile search response SLA.

level: component

  - type: "component"

  - source: "Redis Cache Engine"
    destination: "Enterprise Logging and Monitoring Service"
    description: "Exports telemetry and metrics"

Worker / Background Task Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. The architecture ensures EU data residency and strict <800 ms search performance.

## Key Elements
- Worker / Background Task Container
- Message Broker Container (RabbitMQ / Kafka)
- Distributed Cache Container (Redis)
- External Legacy ILS / Campus ERP Systems
- Observability Sidecar

## Relationships
- Worker Container -> Message Broker Container: Consumes jobs using AMQP / Kafka protocols
- Worker Container -> Distributed Cache Container: Manages locks and state checkpoints using Redis protocol
- Worker Container -> External Legacy ILS: Syncs data using Scheduled Batch Protocols with circuit breakers

## Technology Stack
- Redis: Used for distributed locking, rate limiting, and storing idempotent state checkpoints
- RabbitMQ / Kafka: Powers priority queue partitioning, exponential backoffs, and Dead-Letter Queues (DLQs)
- Protocol Buffers / JSON Schema: Enforces structured payload versioning and backward-compatible data contracts
- Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA): Dynamically scales workers based on queue depth and CPU metrics

## Rationale
Idempotency, circuit breakers, and resource isolation protect fragile legacy systems while preserving worker resources. Queue partitioning and dynamic scaling prevent heavy background syncs from violating the 800 ms search performance SLA.

Observability Sidecars.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive platform for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals while strictly enforcing EU data residency. The architecture integrates robust Observability Sidecars to ensure high performance and strict telemetry governance.

## Key Elements
- Observability Sidecars (OpenTelemetry Collector agents)
- Primary application containers (API Gateway / BFF, Web App, Core Transactional, Search, Workers)
- Enterprise Logging and Monitoring Service (External sink)
- Local encrypted quarantine volume (Dead-letter queue)

## Relationships
- Primary containers to Observability Sidecars: Telemetry data transmission via local `localhost` loops using W3C Trace Context headers
- Observability Sidecars to Enterprise Logging and Monitoring Service: Scrubbed telemetry payload forwarding across network boundaries
- Observability Sidecars to Local Quarantine Volume: Secure routing of invalid payloads via a dead-letter queue (DLQ) strategy
- Prometheus Scrapers to Observability Sidecars: Internal metrics monitoring via Prometheus-compatible endpoints

## Technology Stack
- OpenTelemetry Collector: Standard sidecar pattern for local telemetry buffering and dynamic pipeline reloading
- Prometheus: Endpoint compatibility for internal metrics monitoring (drop counters, queue depth, export latency)
- W3C Trace Context: Standardized protocol for distributed trace-context propagation
- Bounded local disk storage: Spooling mechanism for backpressure management during downstream outages

## Rationale
This architecture uses local sidecars with strict resource caps and circuit breaking to protect the 99th-percentile search response time (<800 ms). Furthermore, local data scrubbing and a fail-open/fail-closed governance matrix ensure strict adherence to EU data residency mandates without compromising system availability.

  - type: "component"
    name: "Prometheus Endpoint"
    technology: "Prometheus"
    description: "Exposes Prometheus-compatible endpoints for internal metrics monitoring such as drop counters, queue depth, and export latency."
  - type: "component"
    name: "Spooling Buffer Manager"
    technology: "Bounded local disk storage"
    description: "Handles backpressure management and data spooling during downstream outages."
relationships:

    description: "Routes invalid or unprocessable payloads to secure local storage via a dead-letter queue (DLQ) strategy"
  - source: "Prometheus Endpoint"
    destination: "OpenTelemetry Collector Agent"
    description: "Monitors internal metrics and operational health"
